name: Pilsner (For Intermediate Homebrewers)

cookwares.name: the basic homebrewing equipment setup and a temperature controlled refrigerator

ingredients.name: water split - blend 4 gallons tap water
11.5 gram packages of dry lager yeast

instructions.primary_message: Line the 7.5 gallon kettle with the mesh bag, fill with 2.5 gallons of tap water and bring to 69°C. Remove from heat.

Mash-in by slowly adding 3.18 kg of pilsner malt into the water and inside the bag. Stir for 2 minutes to prevent balls of grain from clumping together, creating a consistent mash. The temperature should equalize to about 64°C.
Cover the mash, only uncovering to briefly stir every 20 minutes. Heat 3 more gallons of water to 88°C.
After 60 minutes, mash-out by carefully pouring the 88°C water into the mash, stirring to equalize temperature to about 77°C.

Slowly raise the grain bag out of the liquid, allowing the wort to drain from the grain. Hold the grain bag above the kettle for 5 to 10 minutes as the wort drains. Top the wort off with water to 6.5 gallons and add 0.68 kg extra light dry malt extract.
Bring wort to a vigorous boil. When the boil begins, add 43 g Saaz hops in a mesh bag.
After boiling for 70 minutes, add 28 g Saaz hops in a mesh bag.
After boiling for 85 minutes, add 43 g Saaz hops in a mesh bag.

After total of 90 minutes of boil, remove from heat and add 28 g Saaz hops in a mesh bag. Warning: After wort cools below 82°C everything that touches it should be sanitary, and exposure to open air should be limited as much as possible.

Cool wort by placing pot in ice bath or by using a wort chiller until it is below 21°C. Transfer to sanitized fermentor (either a carboy or a fermentation bucket) and place in a temperature-controlled refrigerator set to 9°C (9°C).

Use a sanitized auto-siphon racking cane to remove enough wort to take a gravity reading with your hydrometer. Make a note of this number, since you will be using it to calculate the actual alcohol content when it's done fermenting. The reading should be around 1.054. Cover fermentor with a sanitized stopper and airlock.
After wort cools to 10°C, agitate vigorously for at least 5 minutes. Add two 11.5-gram packages of Saflager S-23 yeast.
Ferment for at least 3 weeks at 9°C (9°C).
After fermentation is complete, rack to a sanitized secondary carboy and allow the beer to raise to room temperature for 12 hours for a diacetyl rest.
Lager for 4 to 6 weeks by placing carboy in a temperature-controlled refrigerator set to 2°C (2°C).
Bottle after lagering is complete, using enough priming sugar for a medium level of carbonation.

description: This is an all-grain homebrewing recipe which is written for the intermediate level, brew-in-a-bag homebrewer. Since this beer is a lager style, it's highly recommended that you have a temperature controlled refrigerator you can use for cold fermentation and lagering.
author: Joe Postma
